## Acceleration and Software
Organizations must shift from big projects to small teams working in short cycles with user feedback. Acceleration is required to deliver value, detect demand, anticipate compliance, and respond to risks. Software drives this: banks trade faster/discover channels; retailers offer fast checkout/recommendations; government serves efficiently. James Bessen (2017) found tech explains revenue/productivity gains more than M&A or entrepreneurship; McAfee and Brynjolfsson (2008) linked tech to profitability.

## DevOps Adoption and Disconnects
DevOps emerged to build secure, resilient, rapidly evolving distributed systems at scale. Adopters include Netflix, Amazon, Google, Facebook, Capital One, Target, and the US Federal Government’s Technology Transformation Service and US Digital Service.
However, gaps persist. Forrester (Stroud et al. 2017) found 31% lack necessary practices (CI/CD, Lean, collaborative culture). Gartner (Panetta 2017) found 47% of CEOs face board pressure to digitally transform. Forrester (Klavens et al. 2017) notes organizations overestimate DevOps progress, especially executives versus practitioners. This disconnect means value potential is greater than realized, necessitating accurate capability measurement to inform strategy.

## Capabilities vs. Maturity Models
Maturity models are inadequate for four reasons: (1) They imply an end state ("arrive"), whereas capability models demand continuous improvement; (2) They are lock-step/linear, assuming uniform levels, while capability models are multidimensional and customized to team context and constraints; (3) They measure tooling install base (vanity metrics) without tying to outcomes, whereas capability models are outcome-based; (4) They define static levels, ignoring that industry standards shift, while capability models adapt dynamically.

## Evidence-Based Performance Drivers
Vendors and consultants often push biased capabilities. Evidence shows app age/tech (mainframe vs. greenfield), who deploys (ops vs. dev), and Change Approval Boards (CABs) do not predict performance. Instead, 24 key capabilities drive software delivery and organizational performance (profitability, market share).
In 2017, high vs low performers achieved: 46x more frequent deployments, 440x faster lead time, 170x faster MTTR, and 5x lower change failure rate. Compared to 2016, the tempo gap narrowed but the stability gap widened. Low performers likely increased tempo without building in quality, causing larger failures. High performers achieve both speed and stability by building in quality.
